sheet-1.description: The lower half of Sheet 1, below the key map and street index, shows the hamlet of Wortendyke on the western edge of Midland Park, mostly in Franklin Township outside the borough. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and is turned on the page, with north towards the upper left. Greenwood Avenue runs along the top edge, where the lower ends of Clinton Avenue, Central Avenue, Park Avenue and Irving Street are lettered as they leave for Sheet 2. Below it the New York, Susquehanna and Western Railroad crosses the sheet with several tracks, the Wortendyke passenger station and freight house, a cement works house and a coal shed. A brook crosses from the left and passes under Greenwood Avenue. Newtown Road, also lettered Central Avenue where it runs south, crosses the railroad and meets Cedar Hill Avenue, which turns at a right angle along the left edge. Hillside Avenue runs across the lower part to Grove Street on the right, and West Street and Railroad Avenue leave towards the north-east beside the railroad. The borough limit runs diagonally across the sheet. Development is sparse: a row of small frame dwellings along Greenwood Avenue, one of them marked as a fire ruin, scattered dwellings on Cedar Hill Avenue and along Hillside Avenue, and large open blocks numbered 34, 48, 306 and 313. A large compass rose sits in the open block east of Newtown Road.
notes: Newtown Road is lettered 'Central Av. or Newtown Rd' south of Cedar Hill Avenue; the modern street is Newtown Road.
Cedar Hill Avenue is Cedarhill Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Greenwood Avenue / Grove Street was left out of the control: the drawn junction is about 7 m from the modern one.
Wortendyke passenger station and freight house on the N.Y.S.&W. R.R.

sheet-2-1.description: Part 1 of Sheet 2 is the main map of the north-western part of Midland Park, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Park Avenue runs up the middle of the sheet and Irving Street parallel to it on the right, crossed by 5th, 4th, 3rd, 2nd and 1st Streets and by Godwin Avenue. Orchard runs along the right edge. To the left, Lincoln or Linwood Avenue crosses Myrtle Avenue, and Godwin Avenue continues down to Clinton Avenue and Central Avenue, with Franklin Avenue, Madison Avenue and Greenwood Avenue across the bottom. Most of the area is laid out in large numbered blocks (25A to 25G, 36 to 47, 50, 51) with scattered frame dwellings; the blocks along 2nd to 5th Streets are largely empty. Christ Church (Episcopal) stands on Godwin Avenue east of Irving. A brook crosses the sheet twice, once from the left past Myrtle Avenue under Godwin Avenue, and once through blocks 37 and 26 near Franklin Avenue and out at the lower right. Water pipes of 6 inches are drawn in Park Avenue, Irving, Godwin Avenue and Central. The top-left corner, framed by a heavy line, is a separate inset (part 2); the triangle above it at the top holds block 44 and the N.Y.S.&W. Railroad. A street lettered 'not named' runs north from 4th Street.
notes: 1st Street is First Street in OpenStreetMap; Lincoln or Linwood Avenue is Linwood Avenue.
Christ Church, Episcopal, on Godwin Avenue.
Central Avenue / Godwin Avenue was rejected by the fit (about 7 m).

sheet-2-2.description: Part 2 of Sheet 2 is an inset in a heavy frame at the top left of the sheet, showing a small area of Franklin Township on the south-western edge of Midland Park, around Sicomac Avenue. Unlike the main map it is drawn with north straight up, at 100 feet to an inch. Sicomac Avenue runs across the inset from the left edge to Railroad Avenue, which runs diagonally beside the N.Y.S.&W. Railroad at the upper right. Hillside Avenue crosses Sicomac Avenue, running north-west above it and south-south-west below it, with a small jog at the crossing. A 25 ft street lettered 'not named' leads south from Sicomac Avenue to Faner Road, which runs east to the frame; a short street lettered Soo (arbitrary) leaves Hillside Avenue near the bottom left. The borough limit crosses the inset diagonally and most of it lies in Franklin Township. Development is light: frame dwellings along Hillside Avenue and Sicomac Avenue, three stone or concrete-block dwellings on Faner Road, and open blocks numbered 27, 28 and 29. Numbers 3 and 6 in the inset refer to the adjoining sheets.
notes: Hillside Avenue south of Sicomac Avenue is Brandon Road in OpenStreetMap.
The street lettered 'not named' running south from Sicomac Avenue is the north-south arm of today's Faner Road; the drawn Faner Road is its east-west arm.
Inset drawn with north up, unlike the main map (about 42 degrees turned).
Placed by three points only (two junctions on Sicomac Avenue and the Faner Road bend); low confidence.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the centre-west of Midland Park around Godwin Avenue and the Goffle Brook, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Godwin Avenue crosses the upper part of the sheet from Orchard on the left to Paterson Road on the right, with Laura Lane (arbitrary), Aqueduct Avenue, Chestnut and Centre and Maple branching north. The Granite Linen Company mill, a large brick manufacturing building with its sprinkler tank, pump and boiler house, stands south of Godwin Avenue on the Goffle Brook, which widens into a pond to the left. The Ridgewood Water Works Wortendyke Station, with its pumping engines described in a note, lies east of Private Road, and the Trinity Reformed Church faces Godwin Avenue near Aqueduct Avenue. In the lower half Greenwood Avenue, West, Cross and Railroad Avenue run beside the N.Y.S.&W. Railroad, with the Standard Oil Company of New Jersey oil tanks on Cross. Hillside Avenue and Birch are at the bottom left; Plane and Lake lie on the right beside Paterson Road. Grove runs along the left edge. Most blocks hold frame dwellings; the land along the brook is open. The brook runs from the mill through a long loop to the lower right, and 12 and 16 inch water mains of the Ridgewood water works cross the sheet.
notes: Laura Lane (arbitrary) is Demund Lane in OpenStreetMap.
Private Road and Cross follow the line of today's Witte Drive, but Witte Drive is 7 to 10 m off the drawn line and was left out of the control.
Lake on this sheet is Morrow Road in OpenStreetMap; Paterson Road is Paterson Avenue; Centre is Center Street.
Maple here lies near today's Outslay Way, which was 13 to 17 m off and left out.
Granite Linen Company; Ridgewood Water Works Wortendyke Station; Standard Oil Co. of New Jersey; Trinity Reformed Church.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 shows the north-central part of Midland Park and the adjoining part of Franklin Township, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Prescott runs up the middle of the sheet from Centre at the bottom to beyond A Street at the top; Chestnut runs parallel on the left and Vreeland Avenue along the right edge, with Woodside Street at the top right. Cross streets are Summit Avenue, B Street and A Street (both private and arbitrary) at the top, Glen Avenue, Chamberlain Place, Payne Avenue, Hill and East Center. Rubble and Dairy run north from Glen Avenue. The borough limit runs across the upper half, and the Franklin Township lettering spans the land north of it. Development is mainly frame dwellings along Prescott, Glen Avenue and Chestnut, with a dense row along Centre at the lower left, where the Dutch Reformed Church stands. Blocks 10, 10A, 10B, 11, 11A and 12 are subdivided into narrow lots, many still empty, especially between Payne Avenue and Hill. Water pipes of 6 inches run in Prescott, Glen Avenue, Hill and Vreeland Avenue. A short street at the left edge is lettered 'not named', and Maple Street leaves Centre at the bottom.
notes: Prescott is Prospect Street in OpenStreetMap.
A Street (private) is Sunset Avenue; B Street (private) is East Summit Avenue; Summit Avenue west of Prescott is West Summit Avenue.
Dairy / Glen Avenue was rejected by the fit (about 8 m).
Dutch Reformed Church on Centre.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the north-east of Midland Park towards the Ridgewood line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Glen Avenue crosses the middle of the sheet from Woodside at the left to Erie Avenue at the right. North of it, in Franklin Township, Highland Avenue, Hillside Avenue and Fairview Avenue run up the sheet between long narrow lots, with Boris (arbitrary), Oak and Monroe Terrace at the upper right and Monroe running along the Ridgewood boundary at the top right. South of Glen Avenue lie Delphine (arbitrary), Chamberlain Place and Payne Avenue, which come in from Vreeland Avenue on the left, and Hill along the bottom. Erie Avenue runs diagonally down to the lower edge, with Sumac Street (arbitrary) and Private Street near it; the strip at the right belongs to the Village of Ridgewood and is left blank with a reference to its map. Development is mostly scattered frame dwellings, with a few concrete-block and stone buildings and a stand pipe of 282,000 gallons on Glen Avenue near Highland Avenue. The borough limit runs across the sheet just north of Glen Avenue. Block numbers 9, 10C to 10E and 11B to 11E mark the subdivisions.
notes: Highland Avenue on this sheet is Highwood Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Hillside Avenue is Van Dyke Avenue near Glen Avenue and Van Dyke Street further north.
Monroe is North Monroe Street; Oak runs on the line of today's Smith Place.
Stand pipe of 282,000 gallons on Glen Avenue.
The North Monroe Street / Smith Place point is hand-picked.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 shows the centre of Midland Park around the Godwin Avenue business street, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Godwin Avenue enters at the top left between Centre and Chestnut, turns at Prospect and runs diagonally to the lower right. East Center, Highland Avenue and Franklin Avenue cross the upper right to Vreeland Avenue on the right edge, where Glen Place also appears. Paterson Road runs down the left side and turns south-east across the bottom, with Lake and Cross coming in from the left and Sicomac Avenue near the Goffle Brook. Pierce Avenue, Pleasant, Blarcom Avenue, Princeton Avenue, Armida Avenue and Habben Avenue fill the newly subdivided blocks 20C to 20G in the lower half, most lots still empty. Institutions include the Midland Park Public School, the Town Hall and Fire Department at Prospect and Godwin Avenue, the Midland Park M.E. Church and the Christian Reformed Church. Industry includes the J.C. Schnoter Co. silk weaving works and the J.E. Cook warping and winding works on Cross, and the Henry Hass Silk Co. mill on the Goffle Brook at Sicomac Avenue. The N.Y.S.&W. Railroad (Erie line) and the brook cross the lower left, beyond which lies Franklyn Township with Faner Road.
notes: Godwin Avenue was left out of the control on this sheet: its junctions were 8 to 12 m from the modern nodes.
Paterson Road is Paterson Avenue; Blarcom Avenue is Van Blarcom Avenue; Armida Avenue is Arminda Avenue; Cross is Cross Avenue; Lake is Morrow Road (left out, about 8 m off).
Township name printed 'Franklyn'.
Midland Park Public School; Town Hall and Fire Dept.; M.E. Church; Christian Reformed Church; J.C. Schnoter Co.; J.E. Cook; Henry Hass Silk Co.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 covers the east of Midland Park between Vreeland Avenue and the Ridgewood line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Vreeland Avenue runs down the left edge, crossed by Hill, East Center, Highland Avenue and Franklin Avenue, with Glen Place at the lower left. Erie Avenue runs diagonally across the sheet from the bottom left to the top right, and Franklin Avenue bends south-east from it to the bottom of the sheet, where Rea Avenue, Cottage Street and Park Avenue come in from Sheet 8. In the upper right Mulder Lane runs east from Erie Avenue and turns south as a second Mulder Lane to Smith Lane; Sumac Street (arbitrary) runs north to Hill at the top right. The land is mostly open: frame dwellings line Hill, East Center, Highland Avenue and Vreeland Avenue on the left, while the large block 7 east of Erie Avenue and block 16 at the lower left hold only a few dwellings and hen houses. A brick building stands on block 16 near Vreeland Avenue. The right-hand strip, beyond the borough limit, belongs to the Village of Ridgewood and is left blank with a reference to its map. Water pipes of 6 and 8 inches run in Hill, Vreeland Avenue, Erie Avenue and Franklin Avenue.
notes: Mulder Lane is Mulders Lane in OpenStreetMap.
Erie Avenue / Highland Avenue and Erie Avenue / Franklin Avenue were rejected by the fit (6 to 9 m): Erie Avenue south of Smith Lane appears to lie off its modern line.
Mulders Lane / Smith Lane was left out: the modern node does not match a clearly drawn junction.

map. Scale 100 ft. One part: Vreeland Av to the Ridgewood line; Hill, E. Center, Highland Av, Erie Av, Franklin Av, Glen Pl, Mulder Lane, Smith Lane, Sumac St (arbitrary), Rea Av, Cottage St, Park Av. Mostly open land.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 shows the south-east of Midland Park around the lower Goffle Brook, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Godwin Avenue crosses the middle of the sheet from Blarcom Avenue on the left to the Ridgewood line on the right. North of it Vreeland Avenue, Erie Avenue, Rea Avenue and Cottage run up to Glen Place and Franklin Avenue; on the right edge the boundary street is lettered Ridgewood Avenue on the Midland Park side and Maltibe Avenue on the Ridgewood side. South of Godwin Avenue are Blarcom Avenue, Habben Avenue and Paterson Road at the left, Goffle Avenue running down to the railroad, and Lake Avenue, which crosses the brook and runs north-east past Cantrell Road, Lakeview Drive and Mountain Avenue. A second Lake Avenue lies beyond the railroad in Franklin Township at the lower left. Industry includes the Henry J. Wostbrock Embroidery Works on the brook, a silk weaving shop on Rea Avenue, a large brick building on Rea Avenue and the Lake Mills with its novelty manufacturing building by the pond. The Midland Park Inn stands at Vreeland Avenue and Godwin Avenue, and the Christian School on Maltibe Avenue. The N.Y.S.&W. Railroad main line, with the Midland Park passenger station, crosses the lower left. The Goffle Brook divides into channels and forms a pond in the middle of the sheet.
notes: Goffle Avenue is Goffle Road in OpenStreetMap; Blarcom Avenue is Van Blarcom Avenue; Paterson Road is Paterson Avenue; Cottage is Cottage Street.
The boundary street is lettered Ridgewood Avenue and Maltibe Avenue; OpenStreetMap has Maltbie Avenue.

The modern Goffle Road / Lake Avenue node lies at the railroad, about 170 m from the drawn Goffle Avenue / Lake Avenue corner; it was excluded. Lake Avenue / Mountain Avenue was rejected (about 14 m) and Godwin Avenue / Maltbie Avenue excluded (about 6 m).
Henry J. Wostbrock Embroidery Works; Lake Mills; Midland Park Inn; Christian School; Midland Park passenger station.
